text:
claire: Quick sync — ran a small bring-up for BlendBench (11B) on int8 vs int6 priming across 5k mixed QA/chat/longform samples. High level notes and proposed next steps below. ping @dmitri @eva

 dmitri: TL;dr: int6 ~= 2.3x cost savings vs fp16 baseline, ~2.0x vs int8. Latency: p50 +10%, p95 + ~40ms. Quality: small regressions concentrated on longform and numeric QA (~1.2-1.8% drop depending on slice).

 eva: Can you paste the slice-level breakdown you mentioned? Curious which tasks lose most.

 dmitri: sure — paste of representative rows from the smoke sweep:
 ```
 slice: longform    int8:0.86 int6:0.84 delta:-0.02 cost_ratio:0.45 p50_ms:120/130 p95_ms:420/460
 slice: shortchat   int8:0.92 int6:0.91 delta:-0.01 cost_ratio:0.47 p50_ms:80/88 p95_ms:220/260
 slice: numeric-q    int8:0.78 int6:0.75 delta:-0.03 cost_ratio:0.44 p50_ms:140/155 p95_ms:480/520
 slice: summarization int8:0.80 int6:0.79 delta:-0.01 cost_ratio:0.46 p50_ms:150/165 p95_ms:500/540
 ```
 note: scores are normalized exact-match/ROUGE-ish on internal eval harness. cost_ratio is int6 cost / int8 cost per-token approximate.

 sara: From product POV — regressions look concentrated on long outputs and numeric reasoning. If we can route short interactive queries to int6 and keep long/numeric on int8, that might be a good compromise.

 vikram: ran a quick routing sim: route rule = tokens_out_estimate <= 512 -> int6 else int8. With traffic profile from last 7 days this yields ~17% unit-cost reduction and overall quality hit ~0.45% weighted. Latency impact on p95 is minor for short queries but visible for longform served on int8 (unchanged).

 claire: Proposed actions: 1) roll a 10% traffic canary A/B for 24–48h using the token-based routing, 2) attach eval hooks for hallucination / numeric-accuracy slices, 3) monitor p95 latency & cost-per-request, 4) test KV-cache priming effects with int6 (might reduce token generation time).

 ops-bot: deploy started: blendbench-int6-canary -> 3 nodes (canary group alpha)

 eva: also suggest trying a prompt-concision micro-test — shorten system priming by 15–25% to see if we can recoup quality while lowering tokens. early tests show prompt len reduction tends to favor int6 cost wins.

 dmitri: i'll spin up the canary config + include the eval slices (longform, numeric-q, shortchat) and a small AB label for hallucination rate. pulling sample split now; will post baseline dashboards and thresholds (alert on >1% quality drop or >10% p95 regress).

 claire: sounds good — thx team. If the canary looks clean we can expand to 50% with gradual rollout. :thumbsup:
